comparison: Perfect agreement. Both evaluate the same claims (C1, C25, C57, C58, C65) regarding MCT1 overexpression in PDAC. Both find the evidence SUPPORTED with strong convergence from RNA-seq and IHC data. OpenEval notes a discrepancy between RNA-seq (~20-25%) and IHC (56%) positivity rates, while peer reviewers accept the findings as 'compelling' and 'solid' without highlighting this discrepancy.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluate identical claims (C5, C33-C38) on serum stability improvements through cyclodextrin encapsulation. Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment of formulation optimization, while peer review emphasizes 'superior stability' and 'convincingly demonstrated' results. No disagreements noted.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluate claims C59-C61 regarding therapeutic window based on differential MCT1 expression between tumors and normal tissues. Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the ~50 TPM threshold is 'approximate' and raises concern about individual variation, while peer reviewers accept without challenge as supporting the selectivity argument.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluate claim C73 acknowledging limitation that ME3BP-7 inhibits but does not cause tumor regression. Both find SUPPORTED as an honest limitation. OpenEval emphasizes this strengthens credibility, peer review notes authors provided 'thorough discussion' of limitations without viewing it as undermining the work.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluate claims C2, C17, C66 regarding clinical context and failure of MCT1 inhibitor AZD3965. Both find SUPPORTED as established background. OpenEval notes specific reasons for AZD3965 failure are not detailed, peer review accepts as providing important context for the novel ME3BP-7 approach.

Agreement with different emphasis. Both evaluate overlapping future direction claims (C74-C79 in OpenEval; C74-C76, C78-C79 in peer review). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN noting these are speculative proposals not tested in the study. Peer review rates SUPPORTED, accepting them as reasonable discussion points that enhance understanding of clinical impact rather than requiring experimental validation.

Strong agreement with different claim groupings. OpenEval R3 evaluates C31, C32, C21 on CRISPR knockout validation. Peer R2 evaluates broader set (C3, C21, C26-C28, C31-C32) covering both knockout and cell line sensitivity correlation. Both find SUPPORTED and emphasize the CRISPR data as convincing evidence of MCT1-dependency. Peer review groups mechanistic validation more broadly.

Partial overlap. OpenEval R2 evaluates C26-C30 on correlation between MCT1 expression and 3BP sensitivity across cell lines. Peer R2 includes C26-C28 but groups them with CRISPR data (C31-C32) and mechanism (C3, C21). Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes correlation and specificity, peer review treats as part of broader mechanistic demonstration.

Strong agreement. OpenEval R6 evaluates C40-C43, C72 on rapid MCT1-specific killing via washout experiments. Peer R4 evaluates overlapping claims C4, C39-C43, C72 (includes potency data). Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval questions whether 'uniquely fast-acting' claim is fully justified, peer review describes evidence as 'compelling' and 'well-designed' without this caveat.

Partial overlap. OpenEval R5 evaluates C39, C4 on preserved targeting specificity and potency after encapsulation. Peer R4 evaluates broader in vitro efficacy including C4, C39-C43, C72. Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on formulation preserving drug properties, peer review emphasizes overall in vitro killing efficacy.

Partial overlap. OpenEval R8 evaluates C47, C48, C6 on anti-tumor efficacy in Panc 02.13 model. Peer R5 evaluates broader set (C6, C47-C49, C55-C56, C80) covering multiple models and overall efficacy. Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes study design details not fully specified, peer review accepts as 'significant anti-tumor efficacy' across models without this concern.

Strong agreement. OpenEval R9 evaluates C49-C52, C7 on anti-metastatic activity in PDX model. Peer R6 evaluates C7, C50-C52 (overlapping subset). Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes mechanism of metastasis reduction not addressed, peer review accepts metastasis data as part of overall efficacy demonstration without this caveat.

Strong agreement. OpenEval R7 evaluates C44-C46, C8 on improved safety of ME3BP-7 vs free 3BP. Peer R7 evaluates same claims plus C53, C62 (tissue-specific safety). Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes toxicity assessment could be more comprehensive with detailed histopathology, peer review emphasizes 'manageable toxicity' and advantage over 3BP without requesting additional data.

Partial overlap. OpenEval R10 evaluates C53, C62 on selective tumor toxicity without normal tissue damage. Peer R7 evaluates broader safety claims (C8, C44-C46, C53, C62). Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes 'no pathological changes of significance' is subjective without detailed scoring, peer review accepts safety data without this methodological concern.

Partial overlap. OpenEval R11 evaluates C54-C56 on efficacy in heterogeneous MCT1 expression tumors. Peer R5 includes C55-C56 as part of broader multi-model efficacy assessment (C6, C47-C49, C55-C56, C80). Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval discusses RNA-protein discordance and reduced efficacy implications, peer review treats as part of overall efficacy demonstration.

Minimal overlap. OpenEval R15 evaluates C3, C18-C23 on 3BP background and mechanism. Peer R2 includes only C3, C21 as part of MCT1-dependency demonstration (with C26-C28, C31-C32). Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval treats as comprehensive background establishing rationale, peer review incorporates mechanistic claims into specificity evaluation.

Minimal overlap. OpenEval R22 evaluates C80-C81 as summary conclusions on therapeutic potential. Peer R5 includes C80 as part of broader efficacy assessment (C6, C47-C49, C55-C56, C80). Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes appropriate qualification with 'potentially,' peer review treats as part of demonstrated efficacy findings.

OpenEval evaluates C24 citing prior proof-of-concept work (Chapiro et al., 2014) for encapsulation approach, finding it SUPPORTED as appropriate background. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - this background citation was not separately assessed by peer reviewers.

OpenEval evaluates C67-C68 comparing ME3BP-7 to ADCs and discussing potential advantages, finding SUPPORTED though advantages are inferred rather than demonstrated. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers did not separately assess these comparative positioning claims.

OpenEval evaluates C69 on broader applicability to other MCT1-expressing cancers based on Human Protein Atlas data, finding SUPPORTED as reasonable speculation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers did not separately assess this broader applicability claim.

OpenEval evaluates C9-C16, C63-C64 establishing clinical context and biological rationale for PDAC metabolic targeting, finding SUPPORTED as standard background. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers did not separately assess these general background claims on PDAC biology.

OpenEval evaluates C70-C71 on speculation about resistance mechanisms and MCT1 not being an oncogene, finding SUPPORTED as reasonable speculation appropriately framed. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers did not separately assess these resistance mechanism speculations.
